newsitem.title: GERMANY: India seen importing 400,000 T sun oil in 96/97.
newsitem.headline: India seen importing 400,000 T sun oil in 96/97.

text.p: India may import 400,000 tonnes of sunflower oil in the 1996/97 (Oct/Sept) season compared with 116,000 tonnes the previous season, the independent Oil World newsletter said.
The publication said the price discount versus groundnut oil and palm olein meant importers were increasingly switching to sunflower oil.
India had already bought large quantities in Oct/April 96/97 from the United States, Latin America, Europe and the former USSR.
This brought its import total for the seven months to 250,000 tonnes versus 11,000 tonnes in the same 95/96 period.
Oil World said per-capita consumption was still low so that low world market prices and domestic income growth quickly translated into gains in imports.
Indian palm oil imports in the four months were 680,000 tonnes versus 560,000 tonnes a year earlier, but soyoil and rapeseed oil imports were lower as a result of sunflower oil's dominance.
Oct/April soyoil imports were 19,000 tonnes, down from 46,000 previously.
India's oilseeds crops should be lower this year, which should also raise the demand for imported oilseeds.
